title: Players on New Teams
brief: Which players changed teams, and is their value likely to rise or fall in the new usage and minutes picture? It must reflect that new-team players often dip in year one unless minutes rise, and flag ripple effects on teammates.
summary: Most players on new teams should be bid at or a little below expert value, because year one usually brings a dip unless minutes rise. The clear exceptions are players whose minutes or role grow, such as Naz Reid, Kel'el Ware, Norman Powell and Peyton Watson. For stars like Giannis Antetokounmpo, LaMelo Ball and Kawhi Leonard, pay the expert price, not the highest site value. On teams with heavy roster turnover (Philadelphia, Milwaukee, Miami, the Clippers), keep FAB ready, because early rotations may not last.

paragraphs.text: The experts agree on the starting point. When a good player moves, his production usually dips. Even stars often take a hit in their first year while they adjust, and growing pains are normal. A star joining a new team tends to lose some value.

In our auction this means one rule: do not pay the highest site value for a new-team star. ESPN's 50 USD for LaMelo Ball and 40 USD for Kawhi Leonard are both called too high. Keep LaMelo to the mid 30s and Kawhi near 24 USD. For Giannis Antetokounmpo, plan around 60 to 62 USD, which is the expert price. Do not chase above it.

LeBron James and Jaylen Brown both moved to Philadelphia. Cap LeBron at 25 USD and do not pay up to his Yahoo rank. Brown is fair at about 23 USD, not the 29 USD our league paid last season. Both fit punt TO builds.

sections.heading: Minutes decide which way value moves

paragraphs.text: More minutes can offset the adjustment hit. A changed role can also raise a player's value a lot, so judge last season's ranks in context. In our league the best new-team values are the players whose minutes rise. Naz Reid needs 31 or more minutes as a starter in Charlotte. Kel'el Ware needs Jenkins to start him or play him 26 or more minutes, which is the gap between a 70s to 80s rank and the top 40s. Peyton Watson has a minutes floor of 30 or more in Cleveland. Norman Powell is valuable only while he stays Chicago's top usage option.

A player moving to a deeper team can lose usage and still gain value, because his minutes and role become more stable. The reverse also holds. A move to a weaker team does not mean bigger numbers by itself, because usage can rise while playing time falls. So for Julius Randle in Brooklyn, check both things: whether his usage really rises toward 30 and whether his minutes hold near 32.

The experts disagree on how much to discount. One side says new-team players, stars included, usually dip in year one and lose value. The other side says usage and minutes changes on a new team can raise value a lot, and that a more stable role can add value even with lower usage. Our plan follows both: discount by default, then pay up only when the new role clearly brings more minutes.

sections.heading: Heavy turnover teams: rotations may flip

paragraphs.text: Teams with a lot of roster turnover tend to be rocky in year one. Adding stars to existing stars has historically been choppy at first. Coaches may try a setup for around 15 games and then reverse it. That makes the back-end fantasy players on these teams uncertain.

Philadelphia fits this pattern. LeBron James and Jaylen Brown join Maxey and Embiid, with Anfernee Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope behind them. Check whether LeBron really plays point guard and gets near 8 assists, and how much usage Brown keeps. Simons and Caldwell-Pope are waiver names only, mainly when Embiid or LeBron sit.

Milwaukee and Miami both reshaped after the Giannis trade, and the Clippers changed after the Kawhi deal. Treat their back-end players as 1 USD flyers or waiver names: Jaime Jaquez Jr., Gary Trent Jr., Bobby Portis Jr., Tim Hardaway Jr., Klay Thompson, Rui Hachimura, Max Strus and Gradey Dick. Do not cut or chase them on week one minutes alone, since the first setup may not last 15 games.

sections.heading: Ripple effects on teammates and old teams

paragraphs.text: The Giannis deal moves value both ways. In Milwaukee, Tyler Herro needs about 34 minutes in a crowded backcourt. Ware's value rests on Jenkins' choices. Jaquez's assists are expected to fall among the many guards. In Miami, Portis holds the minutes behind Giannis and Bam Adebayo, so add him fast if either one misses time.

The LaMelo trade does the same. In Minnesota, check that LaMelo's assists hold next to Edwards and that his minutes reach about 32. Jonathan Kuminga must win starter minutes (around 28) to matter. In Charlotte, Reid gets more usage, but watch his center time next to Diabaté and whether his FG% holds at 45 or better. Royce O'Neale and Grayson Allen only gain if Knueppel and White stay out.

The Boston and Philadelphia swap pushes Paul George into Boston's number two role. Experts expect a top 40 per game return from him at a late-flyer market price. In Boston, Mitchell Robinson's value depends on whether he or Queta starts. Mike Conley matters only if White or Pritchard miss time.

Several old teams open roles. The Lakers' center job is Walker Kessler's, and Sandro Mamukelashvili is his handcuff ahead of Kevon Looney. In Chicago, Powell is the top usage option, and Nic Claxton must hold off Jalen Smith and Zach Collins. In Detroit, John Collins needs 30 to 31 minutes. In Memphis, Isaiah Stewart only matters if Zach Edey misses time. In Denver, DeMar DeRozan needs an injury or trade involving Braun or Johnson.

On 2026-10-18, pay expert prices for the new-team stars and look for value in the 10 to 16 USD range. Good targets are Reid at 10 to 14 USD, Ware up to about 13 USD, Herro at 14 to 16 USD, and George up to 13 USD or a bit more. Kessler is fair at 12 to 15 USD. Fill the last rounds with 1 to 3 USD players whose minutes may rise. Do not pay more than a few USD for Miles Bridges, who every recent expert note calls a bust in Phoenix.

In the first two weeks, check minutes and usage for every new-team player you own. Remember that coaches may reverse a setup after about 15 games. Keep FAB and some of your 6 weekly adds for handcuffs whose role can jump overnight: Portis, Mamukelashvili, Stewart, Andre Drummond and Marvin Bagley III.

Plan around the 2027-03-04 trade deadline. A trade of Powell to a contender would gut his value before our playoffs. Herro also faces trade talk. Consider moving both before the deadline if the rumors grow.
